title: 日本語総まとめ N1 漢字

items.q: 運転免許を（ ）するために自動車学校に通う。
items.qr: Unten menkyo o (___) suru tame ni jidousha gakkou ni kayou.
items.en: I go to driving school in order to obtain a driver's license.
items.why: 免許 (a license) is something you 取得する (acquire); 取材 is specifically about gathering material/information for a news story, not obtaining a document.

items.q: 来年の3月まで日本に（ ）する予定だ。
items.qr: Rainen no san-gatsu made nihon ni (___) suru yotei da.
items.en: I plan to stay in Japan until March next year.

opts.en: a household (noun, can't take する here)

items.why: 滞在する is the verb "to stay/reside temporarily"; 世帯 is a counting noun for a household unit and doesn't collocate with する in this sense.

items.q: テレビの受信（ ）が発生している地区がある。
items.qr: Terebi no jushin (___) ga hassei shite iru chiku ga aru.
items.en: There are areas experiencing TV reception interference.
items.why: 受信障害 is the fixed collocation for signal/reception interference across an area; 故障 describes a specific device malfunctioning, which doesn't fit "地区" (a whole district).

items.q: 宇宙には（ ）の生物が生存する可能性がある。
items.qr: Uchuu ni wa (___) no seibutsu ga seizon suru kanousei ga aru.
items.en: There is a possibility that unknown life-forms exist in space.
items.why: 未知 describes something not yet known/discovered (fits "life-forms"); 未定 describes a plan or schedule not yet decided — the wrong kind of "not yet."

items.q: その記事に対する（ ）は大きく、手紙やメールが500件以上も寄せられた。
items.qr: Sono kiji ni taisuru (___) wa ookiku, tegami ya meeru ga gohyaku-ken ijou mo yoserareta.
items.en: The response to that article was huge — over 500 letters and emails poured in.
items.why: 反響 names the reaction/feedback an audience sends back (matching "500+ letters and emails"); 影響 is a general cause-and-effect influence, not specifically "replies received."

items.q: 日本人は日本（ ）の文化をもっと大切にするべきではないだろうか。
items.qr: Nihonjin wa nihon (___) no bunka o motto taisetsu ni suru beki de wa nai darou ka.
items.en: Shouldn't Japanese people value their own indigenous culture more?
items.why: 日本固有の文化 = "culture native/unique to Japan" — a set meaning for cultural identity; 固定 means physically fixed/fastened in place, which doesn't fit "culture."

items.q: 係員の（ ）に従ってください。
items.qr: Kakariin no (___) ni shitagatte kudasai.
items.en: Please follow the staff member's instructions.
items.why: 指示 is an order/direction that staff give you to follow; 指摘 is calling attention to a mistake or fact — you don't "follow" a 指摘.

items.q: 日本語のクラスは初級、中級、（ ）の3つに分かれています。
items.qr: Nihongo no kurasu wa shokyuu, chuukyuu, (___) no mittsu ni wakarete imasu.
items.en: Japanese classes are divided into three levels: beginner, intermediate, and advanced.
items.why: 上級 names a skill/proficiency level (beginner→intermediate→advanced); 高級 describes luxury or premium quality (a "high-class" restaurant), not a class level.

items.q: 彼は論理的というより（ ）っぽい。
items.qr: Kare wa ronriteki to iu yori (___) ppoi.
items.en: He's less logical than he is argumentative/a hair-splitter.
items.why: 理屈っぽい is a set phrase for someone who over-argues/rationalizes everything; 屈折 is strictly a physical-science term (light bending), never used for a personality trait.

items.q: 他国の内政には（ ）するべきではないとA氏は述べた。
items.qr: Takoku no naisei ni wa (___) suru beki de wa nai to Ei-shi wa nobeta.
items.en: Mr./Ms. A stated that one should not interfere in another country's internal affairs.
items.why: 干渉する is the fixed collocation for interfering in another party's affairs (internal politics, someone's private life); 追及 means pressing/pursuing someone for an answer or responsibility — a different action entirely.

items.q: 自己（ ）に陥る。
items.qr: Jiko (___) ni ochiiru.
items.en: To fall into self-loathing.

opts.en: rejection (of an external request, wrong sense)

items.why: 自己嫌悪 (self-loathing) is a fixed compound describing an inward feeling; 拒否 is an outward act of refusing something someone else offers or asks — it can't attach to 自己 in this way.

items.q: うちの会社では語学の授業料を半分（ ）してくれる。
items.qr: Uchi no kaisha de wa gogaku no jugyouryou o hanbun (___) shite kureru.
items.en: Our company covers half of the language-class tuition for us.

opts.en: bold, daring (wrong part of speech/sense here)

items.why: 負担する means to bear/shoulder a cost; 大胆 describes boldness of character and cannot take する in the sense of "paying for."

items.q: あの人は（ ）で、無駄遣いはしません。
items.qr: Ano hito wa (___) de, mudazukai wa shimasen.
items.en: That person is thrifty and doesn't waste money.
items.why: 倹約家 describes someone who is careful with money; 菜食主義 is about diet, not spending habits — unrelated to "not wasting money."

items.q: 薬を長く飲み続けるのは（ ）場合があります。
items.qr: Kusuri o nagaku nomitsuzukeru no wa (___) baai ga arimasu.
items.en: Continuing to take medicine for a long time can sometimes be dangerous.
items.why: 危険な describes a hazard/risk to health; 真剣な describes a serious attitude or intent, which doesn't fit "a risk to your health."

items.q: 今日は学長の（ ）があります。
items.qr: Kyou wa gakuchou no (___) ga arimasu.
items.en: Today there is a lecture by the university president.
items.why: 講義 is what a professor/president delivers; 購入 means "to purchase" and has nothing to do with a person giving a talk — the two look alike (both コウ, both built on 冓) but are not interchangeable.

items.q: オリンピックで（ ）メダルをとった。
items.qr: Orinpikku de (___) medaru o totta.
items.en: [He/she] won a bronze medal at the Olympics.

opts.en: the trunk of the body (wrong kanji)

items.why: 銅メダル (bronze medal) uses the metal kanji 銅; 胴 means the torso/trunk of the body and never appears in "medal" — the two are pure homophones (どう) with completely unrelated meanings.

items.q: 彼はとても（ ）人で、人を笑わせるのが得意だ。
items.qr: Kare wa totemo (___) hito de, hito o warawaseru no ga tokui da.
items.en: He's a very amusing person, good at making people laugh.
items.why: 愉快な describes a fun, amusing personality; 懸命な describes effort/desperation, not humour — it can't describe someone who makes others laugh.

items.q: 面接で家族（ ）を聞かれた。
items.qr: Mensetsu de kazoku (___) o kikareta.
items.en: I was asked about my family composition in the interview.
items.why: 家族構成 ("family composition" — who's in the family) is a fixed phrase used on job/rental applications; 経歴 refers to one's own career history, a different kind of question entirely.

items.q: 労働に対して（ ）が与えられる。
items.qr: Roudou ni taishite (___) ga ataerareru.
items.en: A reward/compensation is given for labor.
items.why: 報酬 is what you receive in exchange for labor; 応酬 describes a back-and-forth exchange of words (an argument/retort), not payment.

items.q: 携帯電話が（ ）する。
items.qr: Keitai denwa ga (___) suru.
items.en: Mobile phones become widespread.
items.why: 普及する describes something (a product/technology) becoming widely used; 普遍 describes a timeless, universal truth or quality — it doesn't describe a product spreading through a population.

items.q: 突然の出来事に頭が（ ）する。
items.qr: Totsuzen no dekigoto ni atama ga (___) suru.
items.en: One's mind becomes confused by the sudden event.
items.why: 頭が混乱する ("my head is in confusion") describes mental disorder; 混雑 describes physical crowding of people or traffic — a head can't be "congested" in that sense.

items.q: 疲労が（ ）する。
items.qr: Hirou ga (___) suru.
items.en: Fatigue accumulates/builds up.
items.why: 蓄積する means something builds up/accumulates over time — fatigue piling up fits; 消耗する means something is used up/depleted (usually stamina or supplies), the opposite direction of the sentence.

items.q: 国民としての権利を（ ）する。
items.qr: Kokumin to shite no kenri o (___) suru.
items.en: To assert one's rights as a citizen.
items.why: 権利を主張する ("to assert one's rights") is a fixed collocation; 出張 means a business trip and cannot take 権利 as its object at all.

items.q: 隣の国と（ ）を結ぶ。
items.qr: Tonari no kuni to (___) o musubu.
items.en: To conclude an agreement with a neighboring country.

opts.en: a compromise (doesn't collocate with 結ぶ)

items.why: 協定を結ぶ ("to conclude/sign a pact") is a fixed phrase for formal agreements between nations; 妥協 (compromise) describes yielding some ground in a dispute and isn't something you "conclude" with 結ぶ.

items.q: 手術の前に（ ）をする。
items.qr: Shujutsu no mae ni (___) o suru.
items.en: Anesthesia is administered before surgery.
items.why: 麻酔 is what's administered before surgery to numb pain; 摩擦 describes physical rubbing/friction between surfaces — the two share マ but are unrelated to medicine.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: 家賃が安ければ多少の不便は（ ）します。
items.qr: Yachin ga yasukereba tashou no fuben wa (___) shimasu.
items.en: If the rent is cheap, I'll put up with some inconvenience.
items.why: 我慢する means "to put up with/endure"; 自慢 means to boast/take pride in something — the opposite emotional register, and it doesn't fit "putting up with inconvenience."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: 植物の生育を（ ）する。
items.qr: Shokubutsu no seiiku o (___) suru.
items.en: To observe the growth of plants.
items.why: 観察する is what a scientist/student does to plants — watching them closely; 勧誘 means soliciting or inviting someone to join something, which doesn't apply to plants.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: 土地を（ ）する。
items.qr: Tochi o (___) suru.
items.en: To transfer land (to someone).

opts.en: a concession (in a dispute, wrong sense)

items.why: 譲渡する means to formally transfer ownership of property; 譲歩する means to yield/give ground in a negotiation — both start with 譲 but the objects (land vs. a position in an argument) differ completely.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: 来月は会社の（ ）替えがある。
items.qr: Raigetsu wa kaisha no (___) gae ga aru.
items.en: Next month there's a company reorganization.
items.why: 組織替え ("organizational restructuring") is a fixed compound for a company reshuffle; 編集 refers to editing text/media and cannot combine with 替え in this sense.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: 差別や（ ）をなくそう。
items.qr: Sabetsu ya (___) o nakusou.
items.en: Let's eliminate discrimination and prejudice.
items.why: 偏見 pairs naturally with 差別 (discrimination) as a social ill to eliminate; 邪魔 means being physically/practically "in the way," a different register entirely.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 麻・磨・摩・魔

items.q: （ ）な計画を立てる。
items.qr: (___) na keikaku o tateru.
items.en: To make a grand/magnificent plan.
items.why: 壮大な describes something grand in scale/ambition, exactly fitting "a plan"; 娯楽 means amusement/entertainment and can't modify 計画 the way 壮大な can.

items.q: 前言を（ ）する。
items.qr: Zengen o (___) suru.
items.en: To retract a previous statement.
items.why: 前言を撤回する ("to retract one's previous words") is a fixed collocation; 徹底する means to carry something out thoroughly and cannot take 前言 as its object.

items.q: （ ）と供給のバランスを保つ。
items.qr: (___) to kyoukyuu no baransu o tamotsu.
items.en: To maintain the balance between supply and demand.
items.why: 需要と供給 ("demand and supply") is a fixed economic pairing; 補充 means refilling/replenishing a depleted stock, a different concept from market demand.

items.q: 私鉄（ ）のアパートを探す。
items.qr: Shitetsu (___) no apaato o sagasu.
items.en: To look for an apartment along a private railway line.
items.why: 私鉄沿線 ("along a private railway line") is the fixed phrase real-estate listings use; 沿岸 means "along the coast," unrelated to train lines.

items.q: 組織の中で（ ）する。
items.qr: Soshiki no naka de (___) suru.
items.en: To become isolated within an organization.
items.why: 孤立する describes an objective state of being cut off from others (structurally/socially); 孤独 describes the felt emotion of loneliness and is normally used as な-adjective, not with する in this sense.

items.q: 時間は短くても（ ）できればいい。
items.qr: Jikan wa mijikakute mo (___) dekireba ii.
items.en: Even if it's short, it's fine as long as I can sleep soundly.
items.why: 熟睡できれば ("as long as I can sleep deeply") fits a short-but-quality sleep; 徹夜 means staying awake the whole night — the opposite of sleeping at all.

items.q: 水の抵抗を少なくするために船体を流線型にする。
items.qr: Mizu no teikou o sukunaku suru tame ni sentai o ryuusenkei ni suru.
items.en: To reduce water resistance, the hull is made streamlined.
items.why: 抵抗 (Day 3's 氐 group) is read ていこう, "resistance."

items.q: 大雨による土砂災害に警戒が必要です。
items.qr: Ooame ni yoru dosha saigai ni keikai ga hitsuyou desu.
items.en: Caution is needed against landslide disasters caused by heavy rain.
items.why: 警戒 (Day 4's 戒 group) is read けいかい, "caution."

items.q: この野菜は発汗作用がある。
items.qr: Kono yasai wa hakkan sayou ga aru.
items.en: This vegetable has a perspiration-inducing effect.
items.why: 発汗 (Day 2's 干 group) is read はっかん, "perspiring."

items.q: 民間レベルの国際交流に貢献する。
items.qr: Minkan reberu no kokusai kouryuu ni kouken suru.
items.en: To contribute to international exchange at the civilian level.
items.why: 貢献 (Day 1's 工 group) is read こうけん, "contribution."

items.q: その工場の安全管理への懸念が高まっている。
items.qr: Sono koujou no anzen kanri e no kenen ga takamatte iru.
items.en: Concerns over that factory's safety management are growing.
items.why: 懸念 (Day 3's 県 group, marked ❶) is read けねん — note the irregular reading, not "けんねん."

items.q: 骨髄移植手術に成功する。
items.qr: Kotsuzui ishoku shujutsu ni seikou suru.
items.en: To succeed in a bone marrow transplant surgery.
items.why: 骨髄 (Day 6's 隋 group) is read こつずい, "bone marrow."

items.q: 外国人の生活全般に関する相談に応じます。
items.qr: Gaikokujin no seikatsu zenpan ni kansuru soudan ni oujimasu.
items.en: We take consultations regarding all aspects of foreign residents' lives.
items.why: 全般 (Day 4's 般 group) is read ぜんぱん, "overall, all aspects."

items.q: 事件に対する動揺が市民の間に広がっている。
items.qr: Jiken ni taisuru douyou ga shimin no aida ni hirogatte iru.
items.en: Agitation over the incident is spreading among citizens.
items.why: 動揺 (Day 6's 咅 group) is read どうよう, "agitation/disturbance" — note it's a homophone of 童謡 (a children's song) from the same cluster.

items.q: 合唱コンクールで優勝する。
items.qr: Gasshou konkuuru de yuushou suru.
items.en: To win first place in a choir competition.
items.why: 合唱 (Day 6's 昌 group) is read がっしょう, "a chorus."

items.q: 石碑に刻まれた詩を読む。
items.qr: Sekihi ni kizamareta shi o yomu.
items.en: To read a poem engraved on a stone monument.
items.why: 石碑 (Day 6's 卑 group) is read せきひ, "a stone monument."

items.q: 大学では法律をせんこうした。
items.qr: Daigaku de wa houritsu o senkou shita.
items.en: I majored in law at university.
items.why: 専攻 (Day 1's 工 group) means "to major in" — the only option meaning academic specialization.

items.q: この部屋のしょうめいは明るすぎる。
items.qr: Kono heya no shoumei wa akarusugiru.
items.en: This room's lighting is too bright.
items.why: 照明 (Day 2's 召 group) means "lighting/illumination"; 招・紹・昭 share the same component and reading family but form no such word.

items.q: 教材をこうにゅうする。
items.qr: Kyouzai o kounyuu suru.
items.en: To purchase teaching materials.
items.why: 購入 (Day 3's 冓 group) means "a purchase" — 構・講・溝 share the same component/reading but don't combine with 入 this way.

items.q: 仕事の帰りにどうりょうと飲みに行く。
items.qr: Shigoto no kaeri ni douryou to nomi ni iku.
items.en: To go drinking with a colleague on the way home from work.
items.why: 同僚 (Day 5's 寮 look-alike family) means "a colleague" — 寮・療・嬢 are near-identical shapes with unrelated meanings.

items.q: 最近の子どもたちは様々なじゅくへ通っている。
items.qr: Saikin no kodomotachi wa samazama na juku e kayotte iru.
items.en: Children these days attend all sorts of cram schools.
items.why: 塾 (Day 6's 孰 look-alike family) means "a cram school"; 熟 (same family, "mature/ripe") is the classic look-alike trap here.

items.q: 夏は涼しい山の別（ ）で過ごす。
items.qr: Natsu wa suzushii yama no bes(___) de sugosu.
items.en: In summer, [we] spend time at a cool mountain cottage.
items.why: 別荘 (Day 6's 壮 group) means "a villa/cottage."

items.q: 電車の時刻（ ）が改定になる。
items.qr: Densha no jikoku(___) ga kaitei ni naru.
items.en: The train timetable is being revised.
items.why: 時刻表 (Day 3's 表 group) means "a timetable."

items.q: 本日の会議の議（ ）を務めさせていただきます。
items.qr: Honjitsu no kaigi no gi(___) o tsutomesasete itadakimasu.
items.en: I will serve as the chairperson of today's meeting.
items.why: 議長 (Day 4's 長 group) means "the chairperson."

items.q: （ ）気圧の接近に伴い、大雪になるでしょう。
items.qr: (___) kiatsu no sekkin ni tomonai, ooyuki ni naru deshou.
items.en: With the approach of a low-pressure system, there will likely be heavy snow.
items.why: 低気圧 (Day 3's 氐 group) means "low atmospheric pressure."

items.q: 2mもある（ ）大な魚が捕獲された。
items.qr: Ni-meetoru mo aru (___)dai na sakana ga hokaku sareta.
items.en: A giant fish measuring 2 meters was captured.
items.why: 巨大な (Day 2's 巨 group) means "enormous."

items.q: 防犯カメラで店内を（ ）する。
items.qr: Bouhan kamera de tennai o (___) suru.
items.en: The inside of the store is monitored with security cameras.
items.why: Security cameras 監視する (keep watch over) a store for wrongdoing; 鑑賞 is specifically for appreciating art or scenery, not surveillance.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: 関心のある事件の裁判を（ ）する。
items.qr: Kanshin no aru jiken no saiban o (___) suru.
items.en: I sit in on the trial of a case I'm interested in.

opts.en: to sit in on, attend (a hearing)

items.why: 裁判を傍聴する is the fixed collocation for attending a trial as an observer; 防衛 (defence) doesn't pair with 裁判 in this sense.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: 少年少女が（ ）に走らないよう学校と家庭で見守る。
items.qr: Shounen shoujo ga (___) ni hashiranai you gakkou to katei de mimamoru.
items.en: Schools and families watch over young people so they don't fall into delinquency.
items.why: 非行に走る ("to fall into delinquency") is a fixed idiom for young people going astray; 逃亡 means fleeing/escaping and doesn't fit "走らない" in this idiomatic sense.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: 私の故郷は（ ）が盛んです。
items.qr: Watashi no kokyou wa (___) ga sakan desu.
items.en: My hometown has a thriving dairy-farming industry.
items.why: 盛ん describes a thriving industry or activity; 酪農 (dairy farming) fits, while 観客 (spectators, an audience) is not an industry that can be "thriving."
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: この辺は携帯電話の（ ）が届きにくい。
items.qr: Kono hen wa keitai denwa no (___) ga todokinikui.
items.en: Cell phone signal has trouble reaching this area.
items.why: 電波が届く/届きにくい ("signal reaches / has trouble reaching") is the standard collocation for reception; 突破 (a breakthrough) doesn't collocate with 届く.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: ここは駐輪禁止です。（ ）自転車は撤去します。
items.qr: Koko wa chuurin kinshi desu. (___) jitensha wa tekkyo shimasu.
items.en: Bicycle parking is prohibited here. Abandoned bicycles will be removed.
items.why: 放置自転車 ("abandoned bicycle") is a fixed municipal term; 妨害 describes actively obstructing something, not a bicycle sitting unattended.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 放・訪・房・防

items.q: 細胞（ ）を顕微鏡で観察する。
items.qr: Saibou (___) o kenbikyou de kansatsu suru.
items.en: I observe cell division under a microscope.
items.why: 細胞分裂 ("cell division") is the fixed biology term; 行列 (a procession/queue) doesn't apply to cells.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: 税金の格差を（ ）する。
items.qr: Zeikin no kakusa o (___) suru.
items.en: They correct the disparity in taxation.
items.why: 格差を是正する ("to correct a disparity") is a fixed collocation; 既成 describes something already established, not an act of fixing a gap.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: 職場での（ ）を改善する。
items.qr: Shokuba de no (___) o kaizen suru.
items.en: They improve the treatment/working conditions in the workplace.
items.why: 待遇を改善する ("to improve working conditions") is the standard HR phrase; 恩恵 (a blessing/favour received) is something you receive passively, not something you actively "improve."
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: 事件のこれまでの（ ）を説明する。
items.qr: Jiken no kore made no (___) o setsumei suru.
items.en: I explain the circumstances of the case up to now.

opts.en: details, circumstances leading up to something

items.why: 経緯を説明する ("to explain the background/circumstances") fits narrating how an incident unfolded; 相違 names a difference between two things, not a timeline.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: 志望校の（ ）を調べる。
items.qr: Shiboukou no (___) o shiraberu.
items.en: I look up the competition ratio of my desired school.
items.why: 倍率 is the standard term for an exam's applicant-to-seat ratio; 賠償 (compensation for damages) has nothing to do with school admissions.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: レポートを（ ）する。
items.qr: Repooto o (___) suru.
items.en: I submit the report.

opts.en: an embankment (noun, doesn't take する here)

items.why: 提出する is the verb "to submit"; 堤防 (an embankment) is a physical structure and doesn't collocate with a report.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · 違・偉・緯・衛

items.q: 二十歳のとき、人生の（ ）を迫られた。
items.qr: Hatachi no toki, jinsei no (___) o semarareta.
items.en: At twenty, I was forced to make a major life choice.
items.why: 選択 fits an individual's personal life decision; 採択 is used for a formal body adopting a proposal or resolution, not a personal choice.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: 現在の能力を（ ）するよう努力してください。
items.qr: Genzai no nouryoku o (___) suru you doryoku shite kudasai.
items.en: Please make an effort to maintain your current level of ability.
items.why: 能力を維持する ("to maintain one's ability") is the fixed phrase; 支持する means to back or support a person/opinion, which doesn't take "ability" as its object in this sense.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: 物事を（ ）立てて考える。
items.qr: Monogoto o (___) datete kangaeru.
items.en: I think about things in an orderly, systematic way.
items.why: 秩序立てて考える ("to think in an orderly manner") is a fixed expression; 解釈 (an interpretation) is a noun that doesn't pair with 立てて in this construction.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: 自由を（ ）されたくない。
items.qr: Jiyuu o (___) saretakunai.
items.en: I don't want my freedom restrained.
items.why: 自由を束縛される ("to have one's freedom restrained") is the standard collocation; 損失 (a loss, usually financial) doesn't fit "freedom."
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: 道路が（ ）しているので運転に注意してください。
items.qr: Douro ga (___) shite iru node unten ni chuui shite kudasai.
items.en: The road is frozen, so please drive carefully.
items.why: 道路が凍結する ("the road freezes over") is a standard weather/traffic warning; 更迭 refers to replacing a person in a post, unrelated to roads.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: 日本とモスクワの（ ）は6時間です。
items.qr: Nihon to Mosukuwa no (___) wa roku-jikan desu.
items.en: The time difference between Japan and Moscow is 6 hours.
items.why: 時差 specifically means the time-zone difference between two places; 臨時 means "temporary" and has nothing to do with clocks.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 凍・棟・練・陳

items.q: （ ）不十分で不起訴になる。
items.qr: (___) fujuubun de fukiso ni naru.
items.en: The case ends in non-prosecution due to insufficient evidence.
items.why: 証拠不十分 ("insufficient evidence") is a fixed legal phrase leading to non-prosecution; 処分 (disposal/punishment) is not what's described as "insufficient" here.

items.q: 待望の赤ちゃんが（ ）する。
items.qr: Taibou no akachan ga (___) suru.
items.en: The long-awaited baby is born.
items.why: 赤ちゃんが誕生する ("a baby is born") is the natural collocation; 生態 (ecology) describes how organisms live, not the event of birth.

items.q: （ ）が通ると、クレジットカードが発行される。
items.qr: (___) ga tooru to, kurejitto kaado ga hakkou sareru.
items.en: Once the screening passes, a credit card is issued.
items.why: 審査が通る ("to pass a screening/review") is the fixed term for a formal approval process like a credit application; 吟味 means scrutinizing something carefully (words, ingredients) but isn't used for institutional approval processes.

items.q: 二人はかたい（ ）を交わした。
items.qr: Futari wa katai (___) o kawashita.
items.en: The two exchanged a firm handshake.
items.why: 握手を交わす ("to exchange a handshake") is the fixed phrase; 把握 means to mentally grasp/understand something and isn't a physical act you "exchange."

items.q: 参加者の協力によって会は（ ）に行われた。
items.qr: Sankasha no kyouryoku ni yotte kai wa (___) ni okonawareta.
items.en: Thanks to the participants' cooperation, the meeting went smoothly.
items.why: 円滑に行われた ("proceeded smoothly") describes a process free of friction; 単純 (simple) describes complexity, not how smoothly an event ran.

items.q: 税金の医療費（ ）について教えてください。
items.qr: Zeikin no iryouhi (___) ni tsuite oshiete kudasai.
items.en: Please tell me about the medical expense tax deduction.
items.why: 医療費控除 is the fixed tax term for a "medical expense deduction"; 訴訟 (a lawsuit) is unrelated to tax filing.

items.q: 書類のミスを（ ）する。
items.qr: Shorui no misu o (___) suru.
items.en: I correct a mistake in the document.

opts.en: a correction (of a systemic disparity, wrong register)

items.why: 訂正 is used for correcting a specific error, like a typo in a document; 是正 is reserved for correcting a systemic issue such as a wage gap (格差の是正), not a simple document mistake.

items.q: 困難に（ ）してもあきらめないで進む。
items.qr: Konnan ni (___) shite mo akiramenaide susumu.
items.en: Even when facing difficulty, I press on without giving up.

opts.en: a course, route (not a verb-taking noun here)

items.why: 困難に直面する ("to face difficulty") is the standard collocation; 進路する is not a natural verb phrase — 進路 is normally just a noun ("one's path/course").

items.q: 商売が（ ）する。
items.qr: Shoubai ga (___) suru.
items.en: The business thrives.

opts.en: grand, large-scale (describes events, not business as a verb)

items.why: 商売が繁盛する is the fixed phrase for "business thrives"; 盛大 is an adjective describing the scale of an event (a grand ceremony), and doesn't pair naturally with する in this sense.

items.q: 今回の地震で約300人が（ ）になった。
items.qr: Konkai no jishin de yaku sanbyaku-nin ga (___) ni natta.
items.en: About 300 people became victims of this earthquake.
items.why: 犠牲になる ("to become a victim/casualty") is the fixed phrase for disaster deaths; 悲惨 is a describing-adjective ("miserable") and doesn't pair with になる in this way.

items.q: （ ）な毎日が続く。
items.qr: (___) na mainichi ga tsuzuku.
items.en: Ordinary, unremarkable days continue.
items.why: 平凡な毎日 ("ordinary everyday life") is a common fixed phrase; 正直な describes a person's honesty, not the character of one's days.

items.q: 恵まれない子どもたちのために（ ）をささげる。
items.qr: Megumarenai kodomotachi no tame ni (___) o sasageru.
items.en: I devote my whole life to underprivileged children.
items.why: 一生をささげる ("to devote one's whole life") is the fixed phrase; 生存 means the state of surviving and isn't something one "dedicates."

items.q: パスポートの（ ）をする。
items.qr: Pasupooto no (___) o suru.
items.en: I apply for a passport.
items.why: パスポートの申請をする ("to apply for a passport") is the fixed term; 申告 is reserved for declarations like customs or tax filings.

items.q: 地名の（ ）を調べる。
items.qr: Chimei no (___) o shiraberu.
items.en: I look up the origin of a place name.
items.why: 地名の由来 ("the origin of a place name") is the standard phrase; 経由 describes a route/waypoint, not an origin story.

items.q: データを（ ）する。
items.qr: Deeta o (___) suru.
items.en: I analyze the data.
items.why: データを分析する ("to analyze data") is the standard collocation; 分別 usually means either personal discretion or sorting physical items (like waste), not statistical analysis.

items.q: お（ ）にのせてお茶を運ぶ。
items.qr: O-(___) ni nosete ocha o hakobu.
items.en: I carry the tea on a tray.
items.why: お盆 is the physical tray used to carry tea/dishes; お経 is a Buddhist sutra and has nothing to do with carrying tea.

items.q: ゲストは盛大な（ ）で迎えられた。
items.qr: Gesuto wa seidai na (___) de mukaerareta.
items.en: The guest was welcomed with grand applause.
items.why: 盛大な拍手で迎えられる ("welcomed with grand applause") is the standard phrase; 拍子 refers to musical rhythm or a fleeting moment/chance, not a crowd's reaction.

items.q: 事務所のかぎを（ ）する。
items.qr: Jimusho no kagi o (___) suru.
items.en: I lose the office key.
items.why: かぎを紛失する ("to lose a key") is the standard phrase; 粉末 (powder) is an unrelated noun that doesn't collocate with "key."

items.q: これは縮尺1/25000の地図です。
items.qr: Kore wa shukushaku 1/25000 no chizu desu.
items.en: This is a map at a scale of 1/25,000.
items.why: 縮尺 is しゅくしゃく — 尺 keeps its シャク reading from Day 3's 尺 cluster (縮尺, 尺度, 解釈).

items.q: 最先端の技術を駆使した映像がすばらしい。
items.qr: Saisentan no gijutsu o kushi shita eizou ga subarashii.
items.en: The footage making full use of cutting-edge technology is wonderful.
items.why: 駆使 is くし, reusing Day 3's 区・駆 pair (both ク) — 区画 and 駆使 share the same reading.

items.q: 男は殺人未遂で捕まった。
items.qr: Otoko wa satsujin misui de tsukamatta.
items.en: The man was caught for attempted murder.
items.why: 未遂 is みすい, reusing Day 4's 遂 (スイ, as in 遂行) — "attempted but not completed."

items.q: 虫や動物の中には脱皮して成長するものがある。
items.qr: Mushi ya doubutsu no naka ni wa dappi shite seichou suru mono ga aru.
items.en: Some insects and animals grow by shedding their skin.
items.why: 脱皮 is だっぴ — 皮 (ヒ, from Day 1's 皮 cluster: 皮革製品, 疲労, 披露) shifts to ぴ after the small っ, the same sound-change pattern Day 1 warned about with 電波 (でんぱ).

items.q: 今年の新入部員は根性がありそうだ。
items.qr: Kotoshi no shin'nyuu buin wa konjou ga arisou da.
items.en: This year's new club members seem to have grit.
items.why: 根性 is こんじょう — 性 defaults to セイ (性格) but flips to ショウ here, exactly Day 5's "one kanji, two readings" lesson.

items.q: この飲み物は疲労回復に効きます。
items.qr: Kono nomimono wa hirou kaifuku ni kikimasu.
items.en: This drink is effective for recovering from fatigue.
items.why: 疲労 is ひろう, the exact Day 1 homophone pair with 披露 — both read the same way but mean completely different things.

items.q: 1級の試験に挑戦しよう。
items.qr: Ikkyuu no shiken ni chousen shiyou.
items.en: Let's take on the challenge of the level-1 exam.
items.why: 挑戦 is ちょうせん — 挑 keeps チョウ from Day 1's 兆 family, unlike 逃・桃 (トウ) built on the very same 兆 shape.

items.q: その美しい渓谷は観光名所となっている。
items.qr: Sono utsukushii keikoku wa kankou meisho to natte iru.
items.en: That beautiful ravine has become a tourist attraction.
items.why: 渓谷 is けいこく — this question directly tests Day 4's four-way split of 谷 (コク／ヨク／ゾク／ユウ) by offering each wrong reading as a distractor.

items.q: それに関する根拠のないうわさが広まっている。
items.qr: Sore ni kansuru konkyo no nai uwasa ga hiromatte iru.
items.en: A baseless rumor about it is spreading.
items.why: 根拠 is こんきょ — 拠's default reading is キョ (根拠, 占拠); it only becomes コ in the one fixed exception 証拠, which Day 4 flagged with △.

items.q: あの店は安いし、雰囲気もいい。
items.qr: Ano mise wa yasui shi, fun'iki mo ii.
items.en: That shop is cheap, and the atmosphere is nice too.
items.why: 雰囲気 is ふんいき — 雰 keeps フン from Day 6's 分 family, even though the more common member 分析 reads ブン.

items.q: 昔の知り合いとぐうぜん町で出会った。
items.qr: Mukashi no shiriai to guuzen machi de deatta.
items.en: I happened to run into an old acquaintance in town.
items.why: Day 2's 偶・隅・遇 cluster shares グウ, but only 偶 (chance) fits "coincidentally running into someone" — 隅 and 遇 are unrelated meanings sharing the same shape.

items.q: 事故でいしき不明になる。
items.qr: Jiko de ishiki fumei ni naru.
items.en: To lose consciousness in an accident.
items.why: 織・職 both read シキ／ショク and share a component with 識 (Day 2's 識・織・職 cluster), which is exactly why they're tempting distractors for 意識 here.

items.q: 富士山のちょうじょうに立つ。
items.qr: Fujisan no choujou ni tatsu.
items.en: To stand at the summit of Mt. Fuji.
items.why: 停・訂・庁・頂 all share 丁 and could plausibly sound alike to an unsure reader, but only 頂 (a peak/summit) fits "the top of Mt. Fuji."

items.q: 初めて太郎に会ったとき、きょうれつな印象を受けた。
items.qr: Hajimete Tarou ni atta toki, kyouretsu na inshou o uketa.
items.en: When I first met Tarou, I got an intense impression.
items.why: 列・烈・裂 all share 列 and read レツ (Day 2), but only 烈 (intense) fits describing a strong personal impression — 裂 means splitting, and 列 means a queue.

items.q: その国の首相は軍事クーデターでしっきゃくした。
items.qr: Sono kuni no shushou wa gunji kuudetaa de shikkyaku shita.
items.en: That country's prime minister fell from power in a military coup.
items.why: 秩・鉄・迭 all share the 失 shape but read チツ／テツ (Day 3's split-reading family), while 失 itself keeps シツ — 失脚 ("downfall from power") needs 失, not its lookalikes.

items.q: お昼ごはんは（ ）自でご用意ください。
items.qr: Ohiru gohan wa (___) ji de goyoui kudasai.
items.en: Please prepare your own lunch individually.
items.why: 各自 (Day 1's 各・客・格 cluster) is the fixed word for "each person on their own."

items.q: 彼は年上ですが、職場では後（ ）になります。
items.qr: Kare wa toshiue desu ga, shokuba de wa kou(___) ni narimasu.
items.en: He's older than me, but at work he's my junior.
items.why: 後輩 pairs with 先輩 (Day 1's 練習Ⅱ Q8) — 輩 is the fixed kanji for relative seniority in a group, unrelated to age.

items.q: 2（ ）3日の旅行に行く。
items.qr: Ni-(___) mikka no ryokou ni iku.
items.en: I'm going on a 3-day, 2-night trip.
items.why: Day 6's 白 cluster showed both 1拍・2拍 (beats) and 1泊・2泊 (nights) — 泊 is the counter for overnight stays, not 拍.

items.q: （ ）質な豆だけで作った豆腐は味が違う。
items.qr: (___) shitsu na mame dake de tsukutta toufu wa aji ga chigau.
items.en: Tofu made only from high-quality beans tastes different.
items.why: 良質 (Day 2's 郎・朗・浪・廊・良 cluster, where 良 breaks from ロウ to リョウ) is the fixed word for "good quality," here read as an adjectival prefix.

items.q: 学生（ ）を見せてください。
items.qr: Gakusei (___) o misete kudasai.
items.en: Please show your student ID.
items.why: 証 (Day 5's 正・政・征・証・症 cluster) is the fixed kanji for an official certificate/card — 学生証 is the standard term for a student ID.

items.q: 偶然が（ ）、すばらしい商品が開発された。
items.qr: Guuzen ga (___), subarashii shouhin ga kaihatsu sareta.
items.en: A string of coincidences overlapped, and a wonderful product was developed.

opts.en: forming a row/range (wrong — for physical lines, not events)

items.why: 重なる describes events/coincidences stacking on top of each other; 連なる describes physical things (mountains, a line of people) forming a continuous row — it can't take an abstract subject like 偶然.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: 彼は何か家庭に問題を（ ）いるようだ。
items.qr: Kare wa nanika katei ni mondai o (___) iru you da.
items.en: He seems to be carrying some kind of family problem.

opts.en: forcing (someone to do something) — wrong, needs an object being forced

items.why: 問題を抱える is the fixed way to say "to be burdened with/carrying a problem"; 強いる needs a person being forced to do something, which doesn't fit "問題".
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: 秋の青空に赤い木の実が（ ）美しい。
items.qr: Aki no aozora ni akai ki no mi ga (___) utsukushii.
items.en: The red berries stand out beautifully against the blue autumn sky.

opts.en: standing out/looking brilliant against a background

items.why: 生える and 映える are true homophones (both はえる). The berries aren't sprouting — they're contrasting beautifully with the sky, which is exactly what 映える describes.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: これを（ ）と、もうチャンスはないだろう。
items.qr: Kore o (___) to, mou chansu wa nai darou.
items.en: If you let this slip, there probably won't be another chance.

opts.en: remove, take off (wrong object — chances aren't "removed")

items.why: チャンスを逃す ("miss a chance") is the fixed collocation; 外す is for physically removing something (buttons, a seat) and doesn't pair with チャンス.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: 娘が心を（ ）しまった原因がわからない。
items.qr: Musume ga kokoro o (___) shimatta gen'in ga wakaranai.
items.en: I don't know the reason my daughter has shut her heart off.

opts.en: touching (wrong — doesn't fit 心を…しまう)

items.why: 心を閉ざす is the set phrase for emotionally shutting oneself off; 触れる means "to touch," which doesn't combine naturally with 心を…しまう here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: 大学院の専門を（ ）職に就く。
items.qr: Daigakuin no senmon o (___) shoku ni tsuku.
items.en: To take a job that makes use of one's graduate-school specialty.

opts.en: relied on (an odd fit — a job doesn't "rely on" a specialty)

items.why: 専門を生かした職 ("a job that puts one's specialty to use") is a common set phrase; 頼る (rely on) is for depending on a person or thing for support, not for describing how a job uses a skill.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 生かす・生やす

items.q: 締め切りが近付いて気持ちばかり（ ）。
items.qr: Shimekiri ga chikazuite kimochi bakari (___).
items.en: As the deadline approaches, I just feel more and more impatient/anxious.

opts.en: to burn (a pot) — wrong, feelings don't burn

items.why: 気持ちが焦る is the set way to describe inner impatience; 焦げる only applies to something physically scorching/burning.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: 住宅の売買契約を（ ）。
items.qr: Juutaku no baibai keiyaku o (___).
items.en: To sign/exchange a house sale-and-purchase contract.

opts.en: to mix in/exchange views (wrong object — contracts aren't "mixed in")

items.why: 契約を交わす is the fixed collocation for signing a contract between two parties; 交える is for mixing in an element (like opinions) within a larger activity.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: この島は漁業が（ ）。
items.qr: Kono shima wa gyogyou ga (___).
items.en: This island's fishing industry is thriving.

opts.en: at its peak (wrong grammatical fit for an industry's general state)

items.why: 漁業が盛んだ describes an industry generally thriving; 盛り describes a specific peak moment (the height of summer, a peak age) rather than an ongoing state.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: 桜が咲くと、公園全体がピンク色に（ ）。
items.qr: Sakura ga saku to, kouen zentai ga pinku-iro ni (___).
items.en: When the cherry blossoms bloom, the whole park is dyed pink.

opts.en: to be dyed, take on a color (a wide area)
to seep/sting into (a small, localized point) — wrong scale

items.why: 染まる describes a whole area taking on a color; 染みる describes something seeping into a specific small point (like smoke into eyes), which doesn't fit "the whole park."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: このボールペンは（ ）に書ける。
items.qr: Kono boorupen wa (___) ni kakeru.
items.en: This ballpoint pen writes smoothly.
items.why: 滑らかに書ける describes smooth writing motion; 厳か describes solemnity in a ceremony, entirely unrelated to how a pen writes.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: チームは周囲の予想を（ ）優勝した。
items.qr: Chiimu wa shuui no yosou o (___) yuushou shita.
items.en: The team overturned everyone's predictions and won the championship.

opts.en: defeating (someone in an argument — wrong object, predictions aren't "defeated")

items.why: 予想を覆す is the fixed phrase for "overturning/defying predictions"; 負かす needs an opponent being beaten in a contest or argument, not an abstract "prediction."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 平たい・平らな

items.q: （ ）気配りができる人を求めています。
items.qr: (___) kikubari ga dekiru hito o motomete imasu.
items.en: We are looking for someone capable of scrupulous, attentive care.

opts.en: peaceful, friendly (wrong fit — describes an atmosphere, not attentiveness)

items.why: 細やかな気配り is the set phrase for meticulous consideration of small details; 和やかな describes a calm, friendly mood (a meeting, a conversation), not a person's attentiveness.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: 本屋は花屋の（ ）向かいにあります。
items.qr: Honya wa hanaya no (___) mukai ni arimasu.
items.en: The bookstore is diagonally across from the flower shop.

opts.en: a view (wrong — not a spatial direction)

items.why: 斜め向かい ("diagonally across") is a set spatial expression; 眺め means "a view/scenery," unrelated to direction.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: 居眠り運転による事故で（ ）命が犠牲になった。
items.qr: Inemuri unten ni yoru jiko de (___) inochi ga gisei ni natta.
items.en: A precious life was sacrificed in an accident caused by drowsy driving.

opts.en: pleasant (wrong — makes no sense with "life sacrificed")

items.why: 貴い命 ("a precious life") is the set phrase for mourning a life lost; 快い describes something pleasant to experience, which cannot describe a life being sacrificed.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: 楽しい音楽を聞いて（ ）を紛らわす。
items.qr: Tanoshii ongaku o kiite (___) o magirawasu.
items.en: Listen to cheerful music to take one's mind off loneliness.
items.why: 寂しさを紛らわす ("distract oneself from loneliness") is a natural, common phrase; 激しさ (intensity, as of rain) has no emotional state to distract from here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: 年の暮れは（ ）。
items.qr: Toshi no kure wa (___).
items.en: The end of the year is hectic.

opts.en: a long time has passed (wrong sense — not about elapsed time)

items.why: 年の暮れは慌ただしい describes the busy, rushed feeling of year-end; 久しい describes a long stretch of time having passed since something, an unrelated sense of "long."
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: もう少しで1位になれたのに、（ ）。
items.qr: Mou sukoshi de ichi-i ni nareta noni, (___).
items.en: So close to taking first place — what a shame.

opts.en: gross, extreme (wrong tone — for criticizing a serious error, not a near-miss)

items.why: 惜しい is the natural reaction to narrowly missing a good outcome; 甚だしい intensifies something negative (a mistake, a misunderstanding) and doesn't fit a near-win.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 憎い・幼い・快い

items.q: 記者が取材のため、事件現場に（ ）。
items.qr: Kisha ga shuzai no tame, jiken genba ni (___).
items.en: The reporter proceeded to the crime scene to gather information.
items.why: 現場に赴く describes going to a location for a purpose (here, reporting); 驚く describes an emotional reaction, not physical movement.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: 取引先の担当者の機嫌を（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Torihikisaki no tantousha no kigen o (___) shimatta.
items.en: I ended up upsetting/damaging the mood of the client's representative.
items.why: 機嫌を損なう ("spoil someone's mood") is the fixed phrase; 賄う is only for managing money/resources, unrelated to a person's mood.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: どうぞ、座布団を（ ）ください。
items.qr: Douzo, zabuton o (___) kudasai.
items.en: Please go ahead and lay out the cushion.
items.why: 座布団を敷く ("lay out a floor cushion") uses 敷く for spreading something flat on the floor; 履く is only for footwear, worn on the feet.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: のどが（ ）ましたね。お茶でも飲みましょう。
items.qr: Nodo ga (___) mashita ne. Ocha demo nomimashou.
items.en: Your throat must be dry. Let's have some tea.
items.why: のどが渇く is the set phrase for "to get thirsty"; 嘆く means to lament/grieve over misfortune, an emotional verb that cannot take のど as its subject.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: あの時計は（ ）いますね。電池を交換しないといけません。
items.qr: Ano tokei wa (___) imasu ne. Denchi o koukan shinai to ikemasen.
items.en: That clock is off. We'll need to change the battery.

opts.en: making up a shortage (wrong — a clock isn't "made up for")

items.why: 時計が狂う describes a clock running inaccurately; 補う is for filling a lack/deficiency, unrelated to mechanical malfunction.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: 神に（ ）、私は不正をしておりません。
items.qr: Kami ni (___), watashi wa fusei o shite orimasen.
items.en: I swear to God, I have not committed any wrongdoing.

opts.en: adoring (wrong — you don't "adore" a god to deny wrongdoing)

items.why: 神に誓って ("I swear to God") is a fixed phrase for a solemn denial; 慕う means to admire/long for someone, an unrelated emotional verb.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 伴う・狂う・誓う

items.q: 町の活性化のために、町民が知恵を（ ）。
items.qr: Machi no kasseika no tame ni, choumin ga chie o (___).
items.en: The residents rack their brains to revitalize the town.

opts.en: to tie with a rope (wrong — 知恵 can't be physically tied)

items.why: 知恵を絞る ("rack one's brains") is a fixed idiom using 絞る's "squeeze out" sense; 縛る only means physically tying something with rope/string.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: （ ）人柄とストレートな話しぶりで人気のタレント。
items.qr: (___) hitogara to sutoreeto na hanashiburi de ninki no tarento.
items.en: A TV personality popular for an unpretentious character and straightforward way of speaking.
items.why: 飾らない人柄 ("an unadorned/unpretentious character") is a common compliment; 織る means to weave fabric and has no figurative use for personality.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: 博士は受賞に（ ）までの長い間の苦労を語った。
items.qr: Hakase wa jushou ni (___) made no nagai aida no kurou o katatta.
items.en: The doctor spoke of the long struggle leading up to winning the award.

opts.en: to hold out/persist (wrong grammatical shape here — needs に至るまで)

items.why: Nに至るまで ("up until reaching N") is a set grammatical pattern for describing a process leading to an endpoint; 粘る describes persisting/holding out, a different sense that doesn't fit this に至るまで frame.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: この問題の解決を（ ）のは法律です。
items.qr: Kono mondai no kaiketsu o (___) no wa houritsu desu.
items.en: What's blocking the solution to this problem is the law.

opts.en: is entangled/involved with (wrong sense — a law doesn't "quarrel")

items.why: 解決を阻む ("block a solution") fits a law standing in the way; 絡む describes something being entangled with/mixed up in an affair (often money or a personal dispute), not a formal obstacle.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: この機種はあの機種に比べて、処理能力が（ ）。
items.qr: Kono kishu wa ano kishu ni kurabete, shori nouryoku ga (___).
items.en: This model's processing power is inferior compared to that model.

opts.en: become muddy/cloudy (wrong — processing power isn't a liquid)

items.why: 性能が劣る ("performance is inferior") is the natural comparison verb; 濁る describes a liquid/atmosphere becoming murky, unrelated to comparing capability.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: 父は（ ）をしに川や海に行く。
items.qr: Chichi wa (___) o shi ni kawa ya umi ni iku.
items.en: My father goes to the river or the sea to fish.

opts.en: digging (wrong — you don't dig at a river/sea for a hobby like this)

items.why: 釣りをする ("to go fishing") is the standard hobby phrase for rivers/the sea; 掘る means to dig (a hole in the ground), an unrelated activity.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 縛る・絞る・殴る

items.q: お酒を（ ）ようにと医者に言われた。
items.qr: Osake o (___) you ni to isha ni iwareta.
items.en: The doctor told me to cut down on alcohol.

opts.en: to train/toughen (the body) — wrong verb for "cutting down" on something
to refrain from, cut down on

items.why: お酒を控える ("cut down on alcohol") is the set medical-advice phrase; 鍛える means to physically train/strengthen the body, an unrelated action.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 新しいビジネスが急成長を（ ）。
items.qr: Atarashii bijinesu ga kyuu seichou o (___).
items.en: The new business achieved rapid growth.

opts.en: provided/created (an opportunity) — wrong object, growth isn't "created"

items.why: 急成長を遂げる ("achieve rapid growth") is the fixed phrase for reaching a significant outcome; 設ける is for setting up an opportunity/occasion, not for describing an achieved result.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 日本代表を（ ）A監督にインタビューをした。
items.qr: Nihon daihyou o (___) Ee kantoku ni intabyuu o shita.
items.en: We interviewed manager A, who leads the Japan national team.

opts.en: to repay (kindness) — wrong verb, a team isn't "repaid"

items.why: チームを率いる ("lead a team") is the set phrase for a manager/coach's role; 報いる means to repay someone's kindness, an unrelated act.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 道端の草花が春の訪れを（ ）いる。
items.qr: Michibata no kusabana ga haru no otozure o (___) iru.
items.en: The roadside flowers are heralding the arrival of spring.

opts.en: taking on (a quality/color) — wrong sense, flowers don't "announce" by 帯びる

items.why: 春を告げる ("herald spring") is a poetic set phrase for signs of a new season; 帯びる means "to take on/carry" a quality (heat, color, a hint of something), a different sense.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 友人のあまりの不運な出来事に（ ）言葉も見つからなかった。
items.qr: Yuujin no amari no fuun na dekigoto ni (___) kotoba mo mitsukaranakatta.
items.en: Faced with my friend's terrible misfortune, I couldn't even find words to console them.

opts.en: to praise (words for an achievement — wrong tone for misfortune)

items.why: 慰める words respond to sadness/misfortune; 褒める words respond to an accomplishment — misfortune calls for the former, not the latter. See the confusion-pairs callout in §3.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 次の語句を（ ）短い文を作りなさい。
items.qr: Tsugi no goku o (___) mijikai bun o tsukurinasai.
items.en: Make a short sentence using the following word/phrase.

opts.en: regretting (wrong — you don't "regret" a word to build a sentence)

items.why: 語句を用いて ("using a word/phrase") is the standard textbook instruction; 悔いる means to regret something, an unrelated emotional verb.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 用いる・率いる・悔いる

items.q: 犯人に言いたいことは、罪を償ってほしいということです。
items.qr: Hannin ni iitai koto wa, tsumi o (tsugunatte) hoshii to iu koto desu.
items.en: What I want to say to the criminal is that I want them to atone for their crime.
items.why: Day 4's 償う (つぐなう) — 罪を償う is the set phrase "atone for a crime."

items.q: 連なる水滴が真珠のネックレスのようだ。
items.qr: (Tsuranaru) suiteki ga shinju no nekkuresu no you da.
items.en: The strung-together water droplets look like a pearl necklace.
items.why: Day 1's 連なる (つらなる) — describes things forming a continuous string, like droplets resembling a necklace.

items.q: 恥ずかしくて目を伏せた。
items.qr: Hazukashikute me o (fuseta).
items.en: Feeling embarrassed, I cast my eyes down.
items.why: Day 6's 伏せる (ふせる) — 目を伏せる is the set phrase for looking down.

items.q: 休憩時間にネクタイを緩めた。
items.qr: Kyuukei jikan ni nekutai o (yurumeta).
items.en: During the break, I loosened my necktie.
items.why: Day 6's 緩める (ゆるめる) — ネクタイを緩める is the natural collocation for loosening a necktie.

items.q: 彼女のハートを射止めたのは一体だれなんだろう。
items.qr: Kanojo no haato o (itometa) no wa ittai dare nan darou.
items.en: Who on earth was it that won her heart?

opts.en: brought down game — this is 仕留めた, a different word/kanji

items.why: Day 6's 射る (いる) gives 射止める its reading いとめる — "to win over/capture." Option 3 しとめた is the reading of a different, similarly-meaning word written 仕留める; matching the given kanji 射止めた requires いとめた.

items.q: 近所付き合いが煩わしい。
items.qr: Kinjo tsukiai ga (wazurawashii).
items.en: Neighborhood socializing feels like a hassle.

opts.en: (not the reading of 煩わしい)

items.why: Day 3's 煩わしい (わずらわしい) — describes relationships/tasks that feel like a burden.

items.q: 子どもの健やかな成長を願う。
items.qr: Kodomo no (sukoyaka na) seichou o negau.
items.en: I wish for the child's healthy growth.
items.why: Day 3's 健やかな (すこやかな) — the set phrase for wishing a child healthy growth.

items.q: 華々しいデビューを飾る。
items.qr: (Hanabanashii) debyuu o kazaru.
items.en: To mark a glorious/splashy debut.
items.why: Day 3's 華々しい (はなばなしい) — describes a glorious, standout achievement or debut.

items.q: 夢に描いた世界が現実のものとなる。
items.qr: Yume ni (egaita) sekai ga genjitsu no mono to naru.
items.en: The world I envisioned in my dreams becomes reality.

opts.en: carried on one's shoulder (wrong word — 担いだ)

items.why: Day 4's 描く (えがく) — 夢に描く means to envision/imagine something, here as a dream world.

items.q: 体を壊して、何よりも健康が第一だと悟った。
items.qr: Karada o kowashite, nani yori mo kenkou ga daiichi da to (satotta).
items.en: After ruining my health, I realized that health comes before anything else.

opts.en: was graciously given (wrong word — 賜った)

items.why: Day 5's 悟る (さとる) — to come to a realization, here about the importance of health.

items.q: ピストルのたまは、幸い体には当たらなかった。
items.qr: Pisutoru no (tama) wa, saiwai karada ni wa ataranakatta.
items.en: Luckily, the pistol's bullet didn't hit the body.
items.why: Day 2's 弾 (たま) — the kun'yomi たま for a bullet uses 弾, the same kanji as 弾く/弾む.

items.q: 弁護士をこころざして法学部に入学する。
items.qr: Bengoshi o (kokorozashite) hougakubu ni nyuugaku suru.
items.en: Aspiring to become a lawyer, I enroll in the law faculty.
items.why: Day 4's 志す (こころざす) — 弁護士を志す is the set phrase for aspiring to a profession.

items.q: 親元をはなれて下宿する。
items.qr: Oyamoto o (hanarete) geshuku suru.
items.en: To leave one's parents' home and live in lodgings.
items.why: Day 6's 離れる (はなれる) — 親元を離れる is the set phrase for moving out of one's parents' home.

items.q: 実現できそうにない目標をかかげる。
items.qr: Jitsugen dekisou ni nai mokuhyou o (kakageru).
items.en: To set/hold up a goal that seems unlikely to be achieved.

opts.en: achieve/attain (wrong word — the goal isn't yet attained)

items.why: Day 6's 掲げる (かかげる) — to publicly put forward a goal/slogan, even before it's achieved.

items.q: キツネやタヌキという動物は人間にばけると信じられていた。
items.qr: Kitsune ya tanuki to iu doubutsu wa ningen ni (bakeru) to shinjirarete ita.
items.en: Animals like foxes and raccoon dogs were believed to transform into humans.
items.why: Day 6's 化ける (ばける) — the classic word for a creature transforming into another form, especially in folklore.

items.q: 生（ ）からといって、魚を料理しない家庭が増えているらしい。
items.qr: Nama (___) kara to itte, sakana o ryouri shinai katei ga fuete iru rashii.
items.en: It seems more households are avoiding cooking fish, saying it smells "fishy."

opts.en: hateful (wrong — doesn't form a real word with 生)

items.why: Day 3's 生臭い (なまぐさい) — "fishy-smelling" is the compound formed with 臭い.

items.q: 私は母が針と糸で（ ）物をする姿が好きだ。
items.qr: Watashi wa haha ga hari to ito de (___) mono o suru sugata ga suki da.
items.en: I like watching my mother sew with a needle and thread.
items.why: Day 4's 縫う (ぬう) — 縫い物 is its cross-referenced compound noun, "sewing."

items.q: 酒を酌み（ ）ながら、商談をする。
items.qr: Sake o kumi (___) nagara, shoudan o suru.
items.en: Discussing business while exchanging cups of sake.
items.why: Day 5's 酌む (くむ) — 酌み交わす ("exchange cups/drinks") is its set compound.

items.q: 味噌ラーメン、大（ ）1つ、お願いします。
items.qr: Miso raamen, oo (___) hitotsu, onegaishimasu.
items.en: One large-serving miso ramen, please.

opts.en: a serving — forms 大盛り "large serving"

items.why: Day 2's 盛る (もる) — 大盛り is its cross-referenced compound, "a large serving."

items.q: 見たかったテレビの番組を見（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Mitakatta terebi no bangumi o mi (___) shimatta.
items.en: I ended up missing the TV program I wanted to watch.

opts.en: failing to (do something) — forms 見損なう

items.why: Day 4's 損なう (そこなう) — 見損なう ("miss out on seeing something") is its compound-verb use, attaching to another verb's stem.

items.q: その女は（ ）電話をかけて嫌がらせをした。
items.qr: Sono onna wa (___) denwa o kakete iyagarase o shita.
items.en: That woman harassed people by making silent phone calls.

opts.en: reticent (a personality trait, not a call)

items.why: 無言電話 is the fixed term for a "silent call" (the caller says nothing) — a known form of harassment. 無口 describes a quiet person's character, not the nature of a phone call.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: （ ）は聞きたくない。今後注意するように。
items.qr: (___) wa kikitakunai. Kongo chuui suru you ni.
items.en: I don't want to hear excuses. Be more careful from now on.
items.why: "I don't want to hear ___, be careful from now on" is a scolding — you refuse to hear someone's 言い訳 (excuse). 言い付け means an order given to someone, or tattling on someone — it isn't something a scolded person offers.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: 電力消費の無駄を（ ）。
items.qr: Denryoku shouhi no muda o (___).
items.en: Eliminate the waste in power consumption.
items.why: 無駄を省く ("eliminate waste") is a fixed collocation; 省みる is reflexive self-examination (自らを省みる) and cannot take "無駄" as its object.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: 中途（ ）な改革ではなく、やるなら徹底的にやってほしい。
items.qr: Chuuto (___) na kaikaku de wa naku, yaru nara tettei-teki ni yatte hoshii.
items.en: I want a thorough reform, not a half-hearted one, if we're doing it at all.

opts.en: extreme (中途極端 is not a word)

items.why: 中途半端 is a fixed four-character-style phrase meaning "halfway, indecisive." 中途極端 does not exist as a word — 極端 (extreme) pairs with other phrasing, not 中途.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: 皇室関係の仕事をする行政機関を（ ）庁という。
items.qr: Koushitsu kankei no shigoto o suru gyousei kikan o (___) chou to iu.
items.en: The administrative body that handles Imperial Household affairs is called the Imperial Household Agency.

opts.en: a palace (宮殿庁 is not a word)

items.why: 宮内庁 (くないちょう) is the actual, fixed name of Japan's Imperial Household Agency. 宮殿 means "palace" (the building) and never combines with 庁.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: 勝った試合のインタビューは監督の（ ）も滑らかだった。
items.qr: Katta shiai no intabyuu wa kantoku no (___) mo nameraka datta.
items.en: In the post-victory interview, the manager's tone was smooth too.

opts.en: clever (describes a person, not a tone)
a tone of voice, manner of speech

items.why: 口調が滑らかだ ("the tone/delivery was smooth") describes how someone spoke. 利口 describes intelligence/cleverness as a trait, and doesn't collocate with 滑らか (smooth).
items.unit: Week 4 Day 1 · 相互・首相・相性

items.q: 子どもの教育費を（ ）するために昼夜を問わず働く。
items.qr: Kodomo no kyouikuhi o (___) suru tame ni chuuya o towazu hataraku.
items.en: (He/She) works day and night to scrape together the children's education expenses.
items.why: 教育費を工面する ("scrape together money for education costs") is the fixed collocation for raising a specific sum; 工夫する means to devise a clever method or idea and doesn't pair naturally with a sum of money.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: （ ）の水害に見舞われる。
items.qr: (___) no suigai ni mimawareru.
items.en: To be struck by an unprecedented flood disaster.
items.why: 未曾有 describes a disaster of a scale never before seen; 有頂天 describes personal elation/joy, which cannot describe a flood.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: トキという鳥は（ ）記念物に指定されている。
items.qr: Toki to iu tori wa (___) kinenbutsu ni shitei sarete iru.
items.en: The bird called the Japanese crested ibis is designated a natural monument.

opts.en: gold (黄金記念物 isn't a word)

items.why: 天然記念物 is the fixed legal term for a protected natural monument (species or site); 黄金 (gold) doesn't combine with 記念物 in this sense.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: 必要な時、その（ ）発行できる1回限りのクレジットカードがあるらしい。
items.qr: Hitsuyou na toki, sono (___) hakkou dekiru ikkai kagiri no kurejitto kaado ga aru rashii.
items.en: It seems there's a one-time-use credit card that can be issued each time it's needed.
items.why: その都度 ("each and every time") describes a repeated occasion; 都合 describes convenience/circumstances and doesn't fit "issued ___ time."
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: この商品の（ ）品にご注意ください。
items.qr: Kono shouhin no (___)-hin ni go-chuui kudasai.
items.en: Please beware of imitation/lookalike products of this item.
items.why: 類似品 is the standard warning phrase for "imitation/counterfeit goods"; 疑似 means "quasi-/pseudo-" (as in 疑似体験, a simulated experience) and isn't used for counterfeit merchandise.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: ハイジャック犯は乗客を（ ）に、燃料補給と食糧を要求した。
items.qr: Haijakku-han wa joukyaku o (___) ni, nenryou hokyuu to shokuryou o youkyuu shita.
items.en: The hijacker took the passengers hostage and demanded refueling and food.
items.why: 人質にする ("to take hostage") is the only sensible fit; 弟子 (an apprentice/disciple) has no relevance to a hijacking scenario.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 2 · 情緒・仮病・天然

items.q: ベテランの店員は（ ）よく商品を包装した。
items.qr: Beteran no ten'in wa (___) yoku shouhin o housou shita.
items.en: The veteran clerk wrapped the product deftly/efficiently.

opts.en: skillful (wrong adverb form: 巧みに, not 巧みよく)

items.why: 手際よく is the fixed adverbial phrase meaning "deftly, efficiently" (手際がいい/よい + よく). 巧み takes a different adverb form, 巧みに — "巧みよく" is not natural Japanese.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: （ ）のたった、炊きたてのご飯。
items.qr: (___) no tatta, takitate no gohan.
items.en: Freshly cooked rice with steam rising off it.
items.why: 湯気が立つ ("steam rises") is the fixed collocation describing hot food/drink; 生地 refers to fabric or unbaked dough, not vapor.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: （ ）と建前を使い分ける。
items.qr: (___) to tatemae o tsukaiwakeru.
items.en: To switch between one's real feelings and one's public stance as needed.

opts.en: a tone (of an instrument, wrong pairing)

items.why: 本音と建前 ("real feelings vs. public façade") is one of the most famous fixed pairs in Japanese social vocabulary. 音色 describes a musical tone and has no relation to 建前.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: （ ）の時報とともに、休憩する。
items.qr: (___) no jihou to tomo ni, kyuukei suru.
items.en: (We/They) take a break at the noon time signal.
items.why: 正午の時報 (the noon siren/time signal) is a real daily custom in Japan; 夜明け (dawn) has no equivalent fixed "time signal" phrase.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: 夫が見るテレビ番組は、（ ）ニュースです。
items.qr: Otto ga miru terebi bangumi wa, (___) nyuusu desu.
items.en: The TV programs my husband watches are exclusively the news.
items.why: 専ら ("exclusively/mainly") describes what someone watches almost without exception. 自ら means "(one)self, personally" and describes who performs an action, not how exclusive a habit is.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: 景気は回復の（ ）を見せている。
items.qr: Keiki wa kaifuku no (___) o misete iru.
items.en: The economy is showing signs of recovery.
items.why: 回復の兆し ("signs of recovery") is the fixed collocation for early indicators of a trend; 炎 (a flame) is unrelated to economic indicators.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 3 · 浜辺・雨具・家主

items.q: （ ）のように車が何台もつながって、なかなか進まない。
items.qr: (___) no you ni kuruma ga nandai mo tsunagatte, nakanaka susumanai.
items.en: Cars are strung together like prayer beads and barely moving forward.
items.why: 数珠つなぎ ("strung together like prayer beads") is the fixed simile for a long, connected line of things — exactly bumper-to-bumper traffic. 小豆 (adzuki beans) isn't part of this idiom.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: （ ）のお子さんをお預かりしています。お心当たりの方は……
items.qr: (___) no okosan o oazukari shite imasu. Okokoroatari no kata wa...
items.en: We are looking after a lost child. If this sounds familiar to you...

opts.en: whereabouts (not a noun describing a child)

items.why: 迷子 directly means "a lost child" — the exact noun this public announcement needs. 行方 means "whereabouts" and cannot itself describe a person.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: （ ）惜しいのですが、そろそろお別れの時間です。
items.qr: (___) oshii no desu ga, sorosoro owakare no jikan desu.
items.en: I'm sad to part, but it's about time to say goodbye.
items.why: 名残惜しい ("reluctant to part, wistful") is a fixed phrase for feeling sad about an ending. 最寄 means "nearest" (usually of a location) and doesn't combine with 惜しい.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: いいお天気で、洗濯（ ）です。
items.qr: Ii otenki de, sentaku (___) desu.
items.en: With such nice weather, it's perfect laundry-drying weather.
items.why: 洗濯日和 ("perfect laundry weather") is a fixed collocation pattern (X日和 = "great conditions for X"). 浴衣 is an article of clothing and has no such usage.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: 交番の（ ）に道をたずねる。
items.qr: Kouban no (___) ni michi o tazuneru.
items.en: To ask the police-box officer for directions.
items.why: 交番 (a police box) is staffed by お巡りさん, who give directions. お仲人さん arranges marriages and has no connection to a police box.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: やっと（ ）が明けたようだ。
items.qr: Yatto (___) ga aketa you da.
items.en: It seems the rainy season has finally ended.
items.why: 梅雨が明ける ("the rainy season ends/clears up") is the fixed seasonal phrase. 雪崩 (an avalanche) collocates with 起きる/巻き込まれる (occurs/gets caught in), never 明ける.
items.unit: Week 4 Day 4 · 田舎・景色・迷子

items.q: 金メダルが取れた（ ）で、ゆうべは眠れませんでした。
items.qr: Kin medaru ga toreta (___) de, yuube wa nemuremasen deshita.
items.en: I couldn't sleep last night from the excitement of winning the gold medal.
items.why: 興奮で眠れない ("too excited to sleep") is a natural cause-and-effect; 余興 refers to a supplementary performance/entertainment at an event and has no "keeping you awake" sense.

items.q: （ ）お時間をいただきまして、ありがとうございます。
items.qr: (___) o-jikan o itadakimashite, arigatou gozaimasu.
items.en: Thank you for your valuable time.

opts.en: respect (尊重 doesn't take な this way)

items.why: 貴重なお時間 ("your valuable time") is the standard polite fixed phrase. 尊重 normally appears as 尊重する (to respect) or 尊重されるべき, not as a plain 尊重な adjective before a noun like 時間.

items.q: （ ）する会社との争いが激しくなってきた。
items.qr: (___) suru kaisha to no arasoi ga hageshiku natte kita.
items.en: The rivalry with competing companies has intensified.
items.why: 競合する会社 ("a rival/competing company") directly matches "争い" (conflict/rivalry). 貿易する会社 just means "a company that trades" and carries no built-in sense of rivalry.

items.q: 車にはいろいろな安全（ ）がついています。
items.qr: Kuruma ni wa iroiro na anzen (___) ga tsuite imasu.
items.en: The car comes with various safety devices.
items.why: 安全装置 ("safety device/mechanism") is the fixed technical term. 衣装 refers to clothing/costumes and has no place in a car.

items.q: 文字や記号の表記を（ ）する。
items.qr: Moji ya kigou no hyouki o (___) suru.
items.en: To standardize the notation of characters and symbols.

opts.en: identical (a state, not a verb of standardizing)

items.why: 表記を統一する ("unify/standardize the notation") is the natural collocation for making a style consistent. 同一 describes two things already being identical/the same — it doesn't function as "to make consistent" in this construction.

items.q: その場は（ ）なムードに包まれた。
items.qr: Sono ba wa (___) na muudo ni tsutsumareta.
items.en: The scene was enveloped in a hostile/tense mood.

opts.en: hatred (a noun, not this adjectival use)

items.why: 険悪なムード ("a tense/hostile mood/atmosphere") is the fixed adjectival phrase for describing tension in a room. 憎悪 is a strong noun for deep hatred and doesn't naturally describe an ambient mood this way.

items.q: チャンピオンも強かったが、さらに上手の挑戦者がいた。
items.qr: Chanpion mo tsuyokatta ga, sara ni joute no chousensha ga ita.
items.en: The champion was strong too, but there was an even more skilled challenger.
items.why: Comparing skill levels between two competitors calls for うわて ("someone better/superior"); かみて only applies to describing stage position, which is irrelevant here.

items.q: その件については目下検討中です。
items.qr: Sono ken ni tsuite wa mokka kentouchuu desu.
items.en: That matter is currently under consideration.
items.why: 目下検討中 ("currently under review") uses もっか ("at present"); めした describes a person's subordinate rank and cannot modify "under consideration."

items.q: 分別のある人なら、そんなことはしないはずだ。
items.qr: (___) no aru hito nara, sonna koto wa shinai hazu da.
items.en: Someone with good sense/discretion wouldn't do such a thing.
items.why: 分別のある人 ("a person of discretion/good judgment") uses ふんべつ; ぶんべつ describes sorting physical items (like garbage) and cannot describe a person's character.

items.q: 色紙に一言ずつみんなでお別れの言葉を書く。
items.qr: (___) ni hitokoto zutsu minna de owakare no kotoba o kaku.
items.en: Everyone writes a farewell message on the autograph board, one line each.

opts.en: coloured paper (wrong object for farewell messages)

items.why: Group farewell messages in Japan are traditionally written on a 色紙 read しきし (a stiff square autograph board), not on いろがみ (ordinary coloured craft paper).

items.q: 生物ですから、なるべく早くお召し上がりください。
items.qr: (___) desu kara, narubeku hayaku omeshiagari kudasai.
items.en: Since this is perishable, please eat it as soon as possible.

opts.en: living things in general (wrong sense here)

items.why: A food-safety label reading "eat soon" refers to なまもの (perishable food); せいぶつ is the biology term for living organisms in general and doesn't fit a food label.

items.q: オランダと言えば、風車小屋とチューリップが思い浮かぶ。
items.qr: Oranda to ieba, (___) koya to churippu ga omoiukabu.
items.en: Speaking of the Netherlands, windmills and tulips come to mind.
items.why: 風車小屋 ("a windmill building/mill") describing the Netherlands' iconic landscape is ふうしゃ; かざぐるま refers to a small handheld paper pinwheel toy, not a building.

items.q: 社員募集。経験の有無は問いません。
items.qr: Shain boshuu. Keiken no umu wa toimasen.
items.en: Now hiring. Whether or not you have experience doesn't matter.
items.why: 有無 always reads うむ; the other options aren't valid readings of this compound.

items.q: 吹雪の後、雪崩が起きた。
items.qr: Fubuki no ato, nadare ga okita.
items.en: After the snowstorm, an avalanche occurred.
items.why: 吹雪 reads ふぶき; none of the other choices are valid readings.

items.q: 差し支えなければ、ご住所を教えていただけませんか。
items.qr: Sashitsukae nakereba, go-juusho o oshiete itadakemasen ka.
items.en: If it's no trouble, could you tell me your address?
items.why: 差し支える reads さしつかえる; no other option is a real reading of this word.

items.q: 江戸時代の情緒が残る町並みを歩く。
items.qr: Edo jidai no jouchou ga nokoru machinami o aruku.
items.en: To walk through a townscape that retains the atmosphere of the Edo period.
items.why: 情緒 reads じょうちょ; ふぜい is a genuine Japanese word but belongs to a different kanji (風情), not this one.

items.q: 世間体を気にしないで思い通りに生きる。
items.qr: Sekentei o ki ni shinai de omoidoori ni ikiru.
items.en: To live as one pleases without worrying about appearances.
items.why: 世間体 reads せけんてい; the other options aren't valid readings.

items.q: 私は日本の相撲に興味があります。
items.qr: Watashi wa nihon no sumou ni kyoumi ga arimasu.
items.en: I'm interested in Japanese sumo.
items.why: 興味 reads きょうみ; しゅみ is a real word ("a hobby") but is written 趣味, a different kanji.

items.q: もう少し効率のいいやり方はないのだろうか。
items.qr: Mou sukoshi kouritsu no ii yarikata wa nai no darou ka.
items.en: Isn't there a somewhat more efficient way of doing this?
items.why: 効率 reads こうりつ; こうそつ mixes up 率's two readings — ソツ belongs to 軽率/統率, not 効率.

items.q: 首相は発言の事実を否定した。
items.qr: Shushou wa hatsugen no jijitsu o hitei shita.
items.en: The prime minister denied having made the remark.
items.why: 発言 reads はつげん; 発's irregular ホツ reading is specific to words like 発作/発足/発起 (Day 2), not 発言.

items.q: 日本の先端技術や美意識を紹介する。
items.qr: Nihon no sentan gijutsu ya biishiki o shoukai suru.
items.en: To introduce Japan's cutting-edge technology and aesthetic sensibility.
items.why: 先端 reads せんたん; the other options aren't valid readings.

items.q: 大掃除は天井から始めよう。
items.qr: Ousouji wa tenjou kara hajimeyou.
items.en: Let's start the big cleaning from the ceiling.
items.why: 天井 reads てんじょう; the other options aren't valid readings.

items.q: 名前のかしらもじを書く。
items.qr: Namae no kashiramoji o kaku.
items.en: To write the initials of one's name.
items.why: かしらもじ is written 頭文字; 顔文字/絵文字 are unrelated real words that merely look similar.

items.q: いっこだてに住む。
items.qr: Ikkodate ni sumu.
items.en: To live in a detached house.
items.why: いっこだて is written 一戸建て — 戸 (a household/door), not 個 (a generic counter), and 建て (built), not 立て (stood up).

items.q: かいがを見に行く。
items.qr: Kaiga o mi ni iku.
items.en: To go see a painting/art exhibition.
items.why: かいが is written 絵画; 階下/開花 both read かいか (one syllable short) and 海外 reads かいがい (one syllable long) — close but different words.

items.q: 店の前に長いぎょうれつができた。
items.qr: Mise no mae ni nagai gyouretsu ga dekita.
items.en: A long line formed in front of the store.
items.why: ぎょうれつ is written 行列; 系列 is a real but unrelated word (a corporate affiliation group) read けいれつ.

items.q: 傘のえに名前を書いた。
items.qr: Kasa no e ni namae o kaita.
items.en: I wrote my name on the umbrella's handle.
items.why: An umbrella's handle (傘の柄) is written 柄, read え in this word — the same kanji whose other readings (へい/がら) appeared on Day 1.

items.q: 家族連れが海（ ）で楽しそうに遊んでいる。
items.qr: Kazokuzure ga umi(___) de tanoshisou ni asonde iru.
items.en: Families are happily playing at the seaside.
items.why: 海辺 (umibe, "the seaside") was named directly on Day 3 as a related form of 浜辺 (hamabe, "a beach").

items.q: この野菜には（ ）毒作用がある。
items.qr: Kono yasai ni wa (___)doku sayou ga aru.
items.en: This vegetable has a detoxifying effect.
items.why: 解毒 (げどく, "detoxification") is Day 5's own word; none of the other kanji forms a real "___毒" compound with this meaning.

items.q: このところ不調だった投手が今日は好投し、（ ）名を返上した。
items.qr: Kono tokoro fuchou datta toushu ga kyou wa koutou shi, (___)mei o henjou shita.
items.en: The pitcher, who had been struggling lately, pitched well today and cleared his tarnished name.
items.why: 汚名返上 (おめいへんじょう, "clearing one's tarnished name") is the fixed four-character phrase introduced on Day 2.

items.q: 面接のスーツの色は紺、グレー、黒などが（ ）難でしょう。
items.qr: Mensetsu no suutsu no iro wa kon, guree, kuro nado ga (___)nan deshou.
items.en: For an interview suit, colors like navy, gray, or black are probably a safe choice.
items.why: 無難 (ぶなん, "safe, unobjectionable") is Day 5's own word, and fits "a safe/inoffensive suit color" exactly.

items.q: 「芝生に入るな」という立て（ ）が見えませんか。
items.qr: "Shibafu ni hairu na" to iu tate(___) ga miemasen ka.
items.en: Can't you see the sign that says "Keep off the grass"?
items.why: 立て札 (たてふだ, "a signboard") is Day 6's own word — the same 札 that also reads さつ for money.

items.q: （a.空き巣 b.鳥の巣）が入らないように戸締まりに注意する。
items.qr: (a. Akisu b. Tori no su) ga hairanai you ni tojimari ni chuui suru.
items.en: Be careful to lock up so that a sneak thief doesn't get in.

opts.en: bird nest (doesn't "get in" through locked doors)

items.why: 戸締まり (locking up doors/windows) is a home-security context, which matches 空き巣 (a burglar); 鳥の巣 is a literal bird's nest and has nothing to do with locking a house.

items.q: 暗かったが、確かに（a.物陰 b.人影）を見た。
items.qr: Kurakatta ga, tashika ni (a. monokage b. hitokage) o mita.
items.en: It was dark, but I definitely saw a human silhouette.
items.why: The verb 見た (saw) needs an object you can visually see — 人影 (the shape of a person) fits; 物陰 names a location (behind something), not a thing you "see" directly.

items.q: 彼女は（a.口が堅い b.頭が固い）から何でも相談できる。
items.qr: Kanojo wa (a. kuchi ga katai b. atama ga katai) kara nandemo soudan dekiru.
items.en: She keeps secrets, so I can consult her about anything.
items.why: Being consultable about "anything" depends on trusting her not to leak secrets — 口が堅い (tight-lipped); 頭が固い describes a stubborn, closed-minded person, which would make her a worse confidant, not a better one.

items.q: 秘書の仕事は（a.気が荒い b.気が利く）人でなければできないだろう。
items.qr: Hisho no shigoto wa (a. ki ga arai b. ki ga kiku) hito de nakereba dekinai darou.
items.en: A secretary's job probably can't be done except by someone who is smart and considerate.
items.why: A good secretary needs tact and quick thinking — 気が利く; 気が荒い (a rough temper) is the opposite of a quality you'd want in that role.

items.q: もう来ないかと思ったころに、やっと彼は（a.姿を現した b.正体を現した）。
items.qr: Mou konai ka to omotta koro ni, yatto kare wa (a. sugata o arawashita b. shoutai o arawashita).
items.en: Just when we thought he wasn't coming, he finally showed up.
items.why: Someone simply arriving late is 姿を現す (to appear/show up); 正体を現す is reserved for unmasking a hidden or disguised true identity — a much more dramatic meaning than "finally arrived."

items.q: （a.効き目 b.網の目）が粗いと、小さい魚は捕れない。
items.qr: (a. Kikime b. Ami no me) ga arai to, chiisai sakana wa torenai.
items.en: If the mesh of the net is coarse, you can't catch small fish.
items.why: 粗い (coarse) modifying a physical mesh size only makes sense with 網の目 (the net's mesh); 効き目 (effectiveness) isn't something that can be physically "coarse."

items.q: 優秀な成績を（a.修める b.努める）。
items.qr: Yuushuu na seiseki o (a. osameru b. tsutomeru).
items.en: To achieve excellent grades.

opts.en: to strive/make an effort (wrong verb for a result)

items.why: 成績を修める is the set collocation for "achieving/earning grades" as a completed result; 努める describes the ongoing effort itself, not the achieved outcome.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: ご報告があって、筆を（a.執りました b.討ちました）。
items.qr: Go-houkoku ga atte, fude o (a. torimashita b. uchimashita).
items.en: Having something to report, I took up my pen (to write it).
items.why: 筆を執る〈執筆〉is the fixed phrase for "taking up the pen to write"; 討つ means to attack or defeat an enemy and has no connection to writing.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: 秋の美しい空を（a.仰ぐ b.澄む）。
items.qr: Aki no utsukushii sora o (a. aogu b. sumu).
items.en: To look up at the beautiful autumn sky.
items.why: 空を仰ぐ (looking up at the sky) needs 仰ぐ, a transitive "to gaze upward at" verb; 澄む describes the sky/water becoming clear on its own and can't take 空を as its direct object here.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: ドラマの主役を（a.納める b.務める）。
items.qr: Dorama no shuyaku o (a. osameru b. tsutomeru).
items.en: To play the leading role in a drama.

opts.en: to pay/supply (wrong verb for a role)

items.why: 主役を務める is the set phrase for "playing a leading role"; 納める is used for paying taxes or supplying goods, not for a theatrical role.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: 駅までの道を（a.謝る b.尋ねる）。
items.qr: Eki made no michi o (a. ayamaru b. tazuneru).
items.en: To ask the way to the station.
items.why: 道を尋ねる is the standard phrase for "asking the way"; 謝る (to apologize) doesn't fit at all — a common trap purely because 謝る and 尋ねる look similar in kana-stripped test formatting.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: 選択を（a.耐えた b.誤った）。
items.qr: Sentaku o (a. taeta b. ayamatta).
items.en: Made a wrong choice.
items.why: 選択を誤る is the set phrase for "making a wrong choice"; 耐える means to endure hardship and cannot take 選択 (a choice) as its object.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 2 · 絶える・耐える・堪える

items.q: 磁石の針が北の方向を（a.指して b.計って）いる。
items.qr: Jishaku no hari ga kita no houkou o (a. sashite b. hakatte) iru.
items.en: The compass needle is pointing north.
items.why: 北を指す is the fixed phrase for a needle/arrow "pointing" at a direction; 計る is for measuring counts or time, not indicating direction.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: 自ら命を（a.絶つ b.犯す）若者が増えている。
items.qr: Mizukara inochi o (a. tatsu b. okasu) wakamono ga fuete iru.
items.en: The number of young people who take their own lives is increasing.
items.why: 命を絶つ is the set phrase for ending one's own life; 犯す pairs with 罪 (a crime) or 法 (a law), not with 命 (a life).
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: 「反対」と答えた人が過半数を（a.締めて b.占めて）いる。
items.qr: "Hantai" to kotaeta hito ga kahansuu o (a. shimete b. shimete) iru.
items.en: Those who answered "opposed" make up a majority.
items.why: 過半数を占める is the fixed phrase for "constitute/make up a majority"; 締める is for physically fastening (a belt, a lid), not for statistical proportions — both share the reading しめる.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: 金を渡して便宜を（a.図る b.謀る）よう指示した。
items.qr: Kane o watashite bengi o (a. hakaru b. hakaru) you shiji shita.
items.en: He instructed [them] to hand over money and arrange favorable treatment.
items.why: 便宜を図る is the book's own fixed phrase for "arranging convenience/favorable treatment"; 謀る is reserved for plotting something like an assassination or coup, and doesn't collocate with 便宜.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: 仕事が忙しすぎて家庭を（a.省みる b.顧みる）余裕がない。
items.qr: Shigoto ga isogashi-sugite katei o (a. kaerimiru b. kaerimiru) yoyuu ga nai.
items.en: Work is too busy to leave any room to attend to family.
items.why: 家庭を顧みる (attending to one's family) is the book's own listed phrase; 省みる is reserved for self-reflection on one's own conduct, not for "attending to" an external thing like family.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: 難病に（a.侵され b.絞められ）ながらも強く生きぬく人々がいる。
items.qr: Nanbyou ni (a. okasare b. shimerare) nagara mo tsuyoku ikinuku hitobito ga iru.
items.en: There are people who live on strongly even while afflicted with an intractable disease.
items.why: 難病に侵される is the set phrase for a disease invading/afflicting the body; 絞める means to physically strangle, which has no place here.
items.unit: Week 5 Day 3 · 攻める・責める

items.q: （a.細菌 b.最近）を培養して研究する。
items.qr: (a. Saikin b. Saikin) o baiyou shite kenkyuu suru.
items.en: Culture bacteria and study them.

opts.en: recently (an adverb, not a lab specimen)

items.why: Only 細菌 (bacteria) is something you can 培養する (culture) in a lab; 最近 means "recently" and cannot be the object of "culture and study."

items.q: 社会（a.補償 b.保障）制度の見直しをする。
items.qr: Shakai (a. hoshou b. hoshou) seido no minaoshi o suru.
items.en: Review the social security system.
items.why: 社会保障 (social security) is the fixed institutional term; 補償 refers to paying compensation for a specific loss or damage, not a welfare system.

items.q: 携帯電話の使用が会議の（a.進行 b.振興）を妨げた。
items.qr: Keitai denwa no shiyou ga kaigi no (a. shinkou b. shinkou) o samatageta.
items.en: Cellphone use hindered the meeting's progress.
items.why: 会議の進行 (the meeting's proceeding) is what phones would disrupt; 振興 means promoting the development of something (a town, an industry), unrelated to running a meeting.

items.q: 若手議員は政界の世代（a.交代 b.新興）の必要性を訴えた。
